setlist.title: Going Down the Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (3 reviews): Hot versions of Cumberland, China Cat Sunflower, and Jack Straw are highlighted; There is a China Cat Sunflower tease into Going Down the Road Feeling Bad [9][13][15]
- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): He's Gone comes out a little lumpy, though everything else is cooked to perfection; Guitar gets weird on He's Gone, but Jerry's vocals are superb and heartfelt [6][7]
- **Playin' in the Band** (1 review): Playin' in the Band is the longest they've played to date, sounding like 1974 [9]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Cumberland Blues, Dire Wolf, and Me and My Uncle sound and feel good [5]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): The Not Fade Away to Going Down the Road to Not Fade Away sequence sizzles [7]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): The Truckin' jam was good enough for inclusion on the Europe '72 album [6]

## The recordings

- **gd72-05-26.sbd.hollister.12758.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 32 songs; 244 min; rated 4.82/5 by 55 [1]. Said about its sound: Audio quality is surprisingly good considering the number of generations involved; The sound is described as incredible for this recording; The recording has gorgeous sound, matching its reputation [1][5][12][13]
- **gd1972-05-26.sbd.smith.94452.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 32 songs; 237 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1972-05-26.sbd.waddell.89641.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 32 songs; 222 min; rated 4.24/5 by 17 [4]
- **gd1972-05-26.sbd.mvernon.5931.shnf**: soundboard; 31 songs; 214 min; rated 5/5 by 6 [3]

## Around the show

- The first set contained nineteen songs, with the band returning after Playin' in the Band [7]
- The first set is amazing, making the second set feel almost unnecessary [9]
- Jerry Garcia saw the empty sound truck and smiled while playing with tears streaming [13]
- The uploader contacted people who filmed the Veneta show to find this tape [2]
- This was their last European night, featuring high energy and finesse throughout [6]
- A wonderful first set is followed by the famous truckin'-other one - morning dew jam [8]
- First half showcases rock and roll, while the central jam combines psychedelic and jazz fusion [11]
- This show gives the 5/10 Amsterdam Other One a run for its money [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-05-26.sbd.hollister.12758.sbeok.shnf**: source: S:MR> DATx5> CD, including patches (see info file for specifics [1]. Also: The original tape broke in the 90s, but a download site was found later; Transfer by David Hollister from MR to DATx5 to CD, including patches [1][14]
- **gd1972-05-26.sbd.smith.94452.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Matt Smith, Jamie Waddell, and Evan K.; source: SBD > Master Reel (film crew feed) at 7 1/2 i.p.s. [2]. Also: Matt Smith supplied the original discs, with cuts patched using existing shnids [2]
- **gd1972-05-26.sbd.waddell.89641.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Todd Evans; source: SBD Reel > DAT [4]. Also: Todd Evans shared the source, with Morning Dew patched from a previously circulating version; The transfer from DAT included most of Morning Dew, with missing portions patched [4]
- **gd1972-05-26.sbd.mvernon.5931.shnf**: transferred by Matt Vernon; source: Master SBD reel > DAT > CD-R >EAC > CDR [3]
